correctness.rationale: For each target color and nonzero argument the root-of-unity filter is exactly 3 or 0, and at zero it is 1. Removing starts 0,−1,−2 from the field sum subtracts at most 27 before division by 27. The 27-term expansion has constant term p; the six one-support terms vanish by character orthogonality; the twelve two-support and eight three-support terms are bounded by √p and 2√p respectively. In the last two cases the polynomial is not a cube because its distinct linear factors have exponents 1 or 2, so the distinct-root version of the Weil bound applies. The error phases all have modulus one, giving 27N≥p−28√p−27. For √p≥29 the lower bound is (√p−29)(√p+1)+2>0. Independently reran the entire finite interval by an Eratosthenes sieve and direct Euler-character values x^((p−1)/3), identifying the first nontrivial value with color 1. This reproduced the 70 eligible primes through 840, all 42 successes between 307 and 840, the full list of thirteen failing primes, and the last failure 283 with just (0,0,0) missing. It also confirmed (2,0,2) is absent at 151 and 163 while (0,0,0) occurs. The next eligible prime is 307. The proof is for eligible prime fields and ordinary starts 1,…,p−3, not a least integer lower bound or a claim for proper extensions. Replay: python3 /workspace/audit_evidence/05-cubic.py.
